opex.note: Selling the chips and running the company; down 8% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring related charges (gains), net
opex.note: A net gain this quarter, not a charge — restructuring ran in Marvell's favor.

footerNote: Marvell guided Q1 FY26 revenue to $1.875B ±5% — over 60% growth YoY at the midpoint.
oneTimers: GAAP results include $147.6M of stock-based compensation and $247.1M of amortization of acquired intangible assets, both excluded from non-GAAP — that is why non-GAAP net income ($531.4M) is well above GAAP net income ($200.2M).

For the full fiscal year Marvell lost $885.0M on a GAAP basis despite the profitable fourth quarter, after $711.8M of restructuring-related charges for the year — mostly asset impairments in earlier quarters.
Restructuring was a net $12.5M gain this quarter, not a charge.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $45.0M, partly offset by $9.6M of interest income and other, net, makes up the $35.4M outside operations.
pngFooterNote: Marvell guided Q1 FY26 revenue to $1.88B ±5%.

sources.label: Form 10-K for the year ended February 1, 2025 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Data Center revenue hit $1.37B — 75% of the company — up 78% YoY as custom AI silicon programs entered volume production and interconnect products grew, and total revenue set a record at $1.82B, up 27% YoY.
takeaways.title: Data Center drove the record

takeaways.text: GAAP net income was $200.2M versus a $392.7M loss a year ago, as operating income swung to $235.2M from a $33.3M loss. Non-GAAP net income was $531.4M.
takeaways.title: Back in the black

takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was $514.0M in the quarter, and Marvell returned $252M to shareholders — $200M of buybacks plus $51.9M of dividends — while guiding Q1 FY26 revenue to $1.875B ±5%.
takeaways.title: Cash kept flowing

verdict: Marvell's revenue hit a record $1.82B, up 27% on AI data-center demand — and GAAP profit swung to $200M from a $393M loss a year ago.
